name: Klangagenda Calendar
author: klangagenda

sections.description:
Displays a calendar (Google Calendar, Apple Calendar/iCloud, Microsoft 365 /
Outlook Calendar, or Konzertmeister – via iCal/ICS link) as an agenda list,
in the style of “date box on the left, title/date/time/location/description
on the right”. No click behavior (no modal, no redirect) – text remains
normally selectable/copyable.

Provided free of charge by KlangAgenda.de – on
Klangagenda.de you can promote your concerts free of charge across your
region, book rehearsal and concert venues, and offer your own space to
others to make better use of it.

All settings (including a detailed step-by-step guide for each calendar
provider) are available in the WordPress backend under the dedicated
top-level menu “Klangagenda Kalender” (with its own calendar icon).

Shortcodes

[klangagenda]
Shows all upcoming events (including recurring ones, e.g. weekly
rehearsals).

[klangagenda_no_recurring]
Shows upcoming events WITHOUT recurring events (e.g. only
concerts/special events, no weekly rehearsals).

[klangagenda_konzerte]
Shows only events whose title contains the word “Konzert” (German for
“concert”, case-insensitive), e.g. “Winterkonzert”, “Sommerkonzert”,
“Adventskonzert”. By default shows neither a date badge nor a
description per event – instead, the description of the first (next)
event is shown once at the top of the whole list.

By default, this shortcode shows no “Buy tickets” button per event.
The attribute ticket_button="ja" turns this on. beschreibung="nein"
hides the intro description at the top, and badge="ja" shows the date
badge per event:

[klangagenda_konzerte ticket_button="ja" badge="ja" beschreibung="nein"]

“(+)”/”(-)” markers (e.g. from Konzertmeister sync) are automatically
stripped from event titles in all shortcodes.

All shortcodes accept an optional count attribute, e.g.
[klangagenda count=”5″]. If omitted, the default count from the
plugin settings is used.

Fixed date window per post (ab / bis)

Normally the shortcodes automatically show the next upcoming events
from now on. For the typical workflow (one post per concert
tour/period; once it’s over the post moves into the archive and a new
post with the next dates is created), there are optional attributes
ab (from) and bis (until) (format YYYY-MM-DD):

[klangagenda_konzerte ab="2026-09-01" bis="2026-09-14"]

This makes this specific post permanently show exactly the events in
this time window – even once they’re in the past. ab and bis can
also be used individually.

“Load more” button

[klangagenda] and [klangagenda_no_recurring] automatically show a
“Mehr Termine” (load more) button below the list whenever more events
are available beyond the currently shown count. Clicking it loads more
events via AJAX (no page reload). The button does not appear on the
[klangagenda_konzerte] shortcode and can additionally be hidden
explicitly via [klangagenda button="nein"].

“orchestriert von klangagenda.de”

Below each event list (or below the “load more” button, if present),
a subtle, light-gray, centered note “orchestriert von klangagenda.de”
appears by default, linking to https://klangagenda.de. This note can
be fully switched on or off in the backend under “Klangagenda
Kalender”.

Recurring events (RRULE)

RRULE processing covers the common patterns (daily/weekly/monthly/
yearly, interval, count, end date, weekdays). Recurring events without
an end date are pre-calculated up to the configured time horizon
(default 12 months), and continued automatically on the next sync.

Ticket button

The button appears when the title contains “konzert” and the
description contains an http(s) link. Only the first link found is
used.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the whole “klangagenda-calendar” folder to
    wp-content/plugins/, or install the plugin directly via Dashboard ->
    Plugins -> Add New.
  2. Activate the plugin under “Plugins” in the WordPress dashboard.
  3. In the backend menu “Klangagenda Kalender” (top level, own icon),
    enter your calendar’s subscription link under “Kalenderlink
    einfügen”. Google Calendar, Apple Calendar (iCloud), Microsoft 365 /
    Outlook Calendar, and Konzertmeister calendars are supported –
    both https:// and webcal:// links work directly. A detailed
    step-by-step guide for each provider is available in the
    “Anleitung” tab.
  4. Save -> the plugin syncs immediately and then automatically every
    30 minutes via WP-Cron.
  5. Insert one of the shortcodes (e.g. [klangagenda]) into a page or
    post.
sections.faq:
Does the plugin cost anything?

No, the plugin is free and provided by KlangAgenda.de.

Which calendars are supported?

Any calendar that offers a public iCal/ICS subscription link: Google
Calendar, Apple Calendar (iCloud), Microsoft 365 / Outlook Calendar,
and Konzertmeister. Both https:// and webcal:// links are accepted
directly.

How often are events updated?

Automatically every 30 minutes via WP-Cron, plus immediately after
saving the settings or via the “Jetzt synchronisieren” button.
sections.changelog:
2.16.1

  • Fix: [klangagenda_konzerte … badge=”ja” beschreibung=”ja”] still showed
    the description as a single one-off intro text above the whole list
    instead of inside each event’s own card below its date/location (the
    position fix for Konzertmeister events only applied to the default
    [klangagenda] shortcode so far). With badge=”ja” the card already shows
    everything like the default shortcode, so the description now also
    renders per event in the correct position there, and the separate intro
    text is skipped in that case to avoid showing it twice.

2.16.0

  • Change: Klangagenda-Hub sync now transmits both configured sources
    together – if a subscribed external calendar link is set, it is still
    pushed, but “Eigene Termine” (own events created directly in the plugin)
    are now ALSO pushed to the hub alongside it, instead of being skipped
    entirely whenever a calendar link is present.
  • New: the category (“Konzert” / “Probenwochenende” / “Sonstige Termine”)
    of an own event is now included when pushing it to the hub.
  • New: if an own event has its own ensemble name set and it differs from
    the central default ensemble name (Einstellungen), it is now sent to the
    hub as the event’s organizer/promoter name.
  • New: the “Besetzung” (cast/lineup) text of an own event is now prepended
    to its description when pushed to the hub, since the hub has no separate
    field for it.

2.15.3

  • Fix: the “Ticket-/Info-Link” field of an own (local) event was ignored in
    the default list view – it only ever showed a ticket button there when a
    link was found inside the description text of a “Konzert”-titled event
    (meant for synced calendars without a dedicated field). The dedicated
    field now always takes priority and shows the button, in every display
    variant.

2.15.2

  • Fix: the 2.15.1 fix only corrected the length of the internal format array
    for the shared-events-cache rebuild, not its order – several fields
    (end date, recurring flag, source, ticket link, image) were still mapped
    to the wrong placeholder, which could corrupt the end date and cause the
    event to be invisible everywhere. Now fully corrected.
  • Fix: creating/editing an own event no longer allows an end date/time
    before the start date/time – the end date now automatically follows the
    start date when creating a new event (until changed by hand), and as a
    safety net the end is clamped to the start if it would end up earlier.

2.15.1

  • Fix: own (local) events created or edited after updating to 2.15.0 were
    silently dropped from the shared events cache and therefore did not show
    up in any shortcode – caused by a mismatched format array in the internal
    cache-rebuild query after the new category field was added.

2.15.0

  • New: central default ensemble name (Einstellungen) – pre-fills the
    Ensemblename field when creating a new event (still overridable/clearable
    per event as before) and is shown as a fallback for events that have no
    ensemble name of their own, including synced/subscribed calendar events.
  • New: category field (“Konzert” / “Probenwochenende” / “Sonstige Termine”)
    when creating an own event, plus two new shortcodes –
    [klangagenda_probenwochenende] and [klangagenda_sonstige] – to show only
    events of that category. [klangagenda_konzerte] now also includes own
    events tagged “Konzert” in addition to its existing title/category
    detection.

2.14.3

  • Changed: restored the clickable “Outlook/Windows” link (webcal://) – it
    does correctly open Outlook’s “Subscribe from internet” dialog, Windows’
    own webcal: handler just pre-fills it with a broken address (missing
    “https:”), a known OS-level bug outside the plugin’s control. The hint now
    explains that and gives the full address to paste in instead.

2.14.2

  • Changed: removed the clickable “Outlook/Windows” link – neither webcal://
    nor a plain https link can reliably trigger a live subscription in Outlook
    on Windows (the https link just downloads the file as a one-time import).
    Only the copyable feed address remains, with instructions for adding it
    manually under “Kalender hinzufügen -> Aus dem Internet abonnieren”, which
    is the standard way to do this on Windows anyway.

2.14.1

  • Fixed: the “Zum Kalender hinzufügen (Outlook/Windows)” link now uses the
    plain https address instead of webcal:// – Outlook strips just the
    “webcal:” prefix when receiving that link, leaving a schemeless URL
    (“//domain/…”) that it then rejects itself as “Ungültige URL”.

2.14.0

  • Fixed: the subscribe feed now has its own clean URL ending in “kalender.ics”
    (instead of “/?klanca_ics_feed=1”) – Outlook’s “Subscribe from internet”
    dialog rejected the previous query-string URL as “Ungültige URL” since it
    didn’t look like an .ics file.

2.13.5

  • Changed: the “Zum Apple Kalender hinzufügen” / “Outlook/Windows” links use
    webcal:// again instead of a plain https download – a downloaded .ics file
    only imports events once, it does not keep them updated like a real
    subscription. Added the feed address as copyable text for manually adding
    it as a calendar subscription when the link doesn’t open automatically.

2.13.4

  • Fixed: the subscribe feed URL could come out protocol-relative
    (“//domain/…”, no “https:”) on sites where a caching/CDN plugin filters
    home_url() – Windows/Outlook showed “Ungültige URL” for that. The scheme
    is now always enforced.

2.13.3

  • Changed: the “Zum Apple Kalender hinzufügen” / “Outlook/Windows” links now
    use the normal https feed URL instead of webcal:// – the webcal: scheme
    had no registered handler in some browsers (notably Chrome), so nothing
    happened on click. Added a fallback hint for manually adding the link as
    a calendar subscription.

2.13.2

  • Fixed: the public .ics subscribe feed (used by the “Kalender abonnieren”
    section) is no longer served via /wp-admin/admin-post.php, which many
    hosting/security setups block for non-logged-in visitors – it now uses a
    normal frontend URL, so the Apple/Outlook subscribe links and the Google
    Calendar import actually work.

2.13.1

  • Changed: the “Kalender abonnieren” toggle is now a plain accent-colored
    text link instead of a bordered button.

2.13.0

  • New: collapsible “Kalender abonnieren” section at the end of the event
    list, with links to subscribe to the whole calendar (all upcoming events)
    in Apple Calendar, Google Calendar, or Outlook/Windows. Backed by a new
    public .ics feed that always reflects the current events. Can be hidden
    via a new setting.

2.12.3

  • Fixed: the “Termin speichern” link no longer gets squeezed next to the
    “Tickets kaufen” button – it now always sits on its own line below it.

2.12.2

  • Fixed: the admin settings preview for the “Detailansicht (aufklappbar)”
    design now uses the same CSS classes as the live site for the
    “Tickets kaufen” button, so the preview’s buttons are the same height
    and aligned like on the actual website.

2.12.1

  • Fixed: the “Nur Stadtname statt ganzer Adresse in der Liste anzeigen”
    setting now also controls the Detailansicht’s overview heading – that
    heading ignored the setting and always showed only the city before.

2.12.0

  • New setting: “Termin speichern” (.ics-Download) can now be shown or hidden
    for all calendar view designs, not just the Detailansicht. Default:
    enabled (previous Detailansicht behaviour is unchanged).

2.11.3

  • Detailansicht design: opening “Details” on one event now automatically
    closes any other event’s details that were still open, so only one is
    expanded at a time.

2.11.2

  • Moved the “Ortsname-Größe (Detailansicht)” setting next to the “Ort”
    setting (short city name vs. full address in the list).

2.11.1

  • Renamed the “Eigene Termine” admin tab to “Termine anlegen”.

2.11.0

  • New settings (Einstellungen-Tab), each like the existing “Terminbeschreibung
    direkt unter dem Termin anzeigen”: whether the Ensemblename and the
    Besetzung show directly in the list, or only in the popup (standard/card
    designs) resp. the expandable area (Detailansicht); and whether the list
    shows only the city or the full address for the location (the full address
    then moves to the popup/expandable area). All three default to the
    previous behaviour, so nothing changes until adjusted.

2.10.0

  • Ensemblename and Besetzung (own events) now also appear in the standard
    and card calendar view designs, not just in the Detailansicht: the
    Ensemblename always shows when filled in, and the Besetzung appears at
    the same place and under the same “Beschreibung direkt anzeigen” setting
    as the description (inline, or together with it in the popup).
  • Renamed the “Ensemblename (kurz)” field to “Ensemblename”.

2.9.5

  • Fixed a bug in the Detailansicht design where the same event shown more
    than once on a page (e.g. additionally in a “next concert” shortcode)
    produced duplicate HTML ids – clicking “Details” on the second occurrence
    then wrongly toggled the first occurrence’s panel instead of its own.

2.9.4

  • Removed the separate “Kurzbeschreibung/Programm” field for own events – the
    “Titel” field is now also shown in the overview of the “Detailansicht
    (aufklappbar)” calendar view design, where the subtitle used to appear.

2.9.3

  • Detailansicht design: the city is now correctly extracted even when the
    location field ends with a country (e.g. “Deutschland”) – that is no
    longer shown as the city.
  • Detailansicht design: the “Details” and ticket buttons are now always
    exactly the same size and aligned on the same line (a leftover margin
    from the generic ticket-button style was pushing the ticket button down).

2.9.2

  • Updated the placeholder examples for the subtitle/program, short ensemble
    name and line-up fields of own events.

2.9.1

  • Detailansicht design: the overview now shows the city name instead of the
    venue name.
  • Detailansicht design: the “Details” and ticket buttons are now always the
    same size (the toggle button no longer shrinks when expanded).
  • Detailansicht design: on mobile, both buttons now stretch to the full
    available width.
  • Detailansicht design: the view now uses the full available width instead
    of the usual 700px reading width.

2.9.0

  • New calendar view design “Detailansicht (aufklappbar)” (“Detail view
    (expandable)”), selectable in the existing “Kalenderansicht” setting:
    weekday/date/time, venue name instead of the usual title, an optional
    subtitle/program line, an optional short ensemble name, a “Details” toggle
    button that expands a panel with location, line-up (“Besetzung”) and
    website/ticket link, and a “Termin speichern” button that downloads the
    event as a real .ics file (generated client-side, no server round-trip).
    Works for calendar-link/hub events too; the ensemble/subtitle/photo fields
    are only available for self-created local events and are simply omitted
    when not set.
  • Own events (“Eigene Termine”) now have a dedicated subtitle field, a short
    and a long ensemble name field, and a rich-text editor (formatting, image
    upload) for the description instead of a plain text field.
  • The venue-name heading size in the new detail view has its own setting,
    independent of the other designs’ title size.

2.8.0

  • Konzertmeister descriptions that start with a category label (“Auftritt -“,
    “Probe -“, “Sonstiges -“, “Probenanfrage -“, “Auftrittsanfrage -“,
    “Information -“) now show only the text after the label – the label itself
    is hidden.
  • An event labeled “Auftritt” is now always treated as a concert (shown in
    [klangagenda_konzerte], eligible for the “Tickets kaufen” button),
    regardless of what the title says.
  • Events labeled “Probenanfrage”, “Auftrittsanfrage” or “Information” are
    internal requests/notes, not public events, and are now hidden from the
    calendar by default. A new setting lets you show them anyway.

2.7.2

  • Fix: when a single occurrence of a recurring event (Google Calendar, iCloud,
    etc.) was moved or edited on its own (“this event” instead of “all events”),
    it could appear twice – once at its old time and once at its new time. The
    moved/edited occurrence is now correctly recognized and shown only once, at
    its new time. A single occurrence deleted this way (without removing the
    whole series) is also now correctly removed.

2.7.1

  • The “Klangagenda Hub” connection now also works in reverse: events created
    directly on Klangagenda.de for your account (e.g. via the online form
    there, not entered in this plugin) are now automatically fetched back and
    merged into your calendar here as well, with duplicate protection to
    prevent an event from appearing twice. Requires Kalender-Hub 8.38.0 or
    later on the connected Klangagenda site.

2.7.0

  • The label text of the “Tickets kaufen” and “Mehr Termine” buttons is now
    configurable in the backend settings. Leave the field empty to keep using
    the previous default text.

2.6.4

  • Fix ([klangagenda_konzerte] only): an all-day event (e.g. an internal
    schedule imported from Konzertmeister) could end up as the detached intro
    description shown once above the whole list, instead of within its own
    event card. All-day events are now excluded from that intro selection and
    instead show their description normally under location/date in their own
    card, like on the other shortcodes.

2.6.3

  • Fix: an own event synced both via the calendar link and via the “Klangagenda
    Hub” venue-events feature (2.6.2) could appear twice in the list. Events
    from the Hub with the same title and start time as an already-synced own
    event are now skipped automatically.

2.6.2

  • New opt-in on the “Klangagenda Hub” tab (only shown if a venue is managed
    there): show events of other organizations taking place at your venue
    (created on Klangagenda) alongside your own events. Off by default; each
    event is labeled with the organizing group’s name.

2.6.1

  • The “Klangagenda Hub” connection now matches the real, already-built Hub API
    exactly (correct base domain, matching endpoints and field names).
  • The venue settings and usage statistics from the Hub are now displayed as
    readable tables in the backend instead of raw data.
  • Fixed a bug where a Hub error response (e.g. “no venue managed”) could be
    mistaken for successful data.

2.6.0

  • New “Eigene Termine” (own events) tab: create events directly in the plugin
    backend, with no external calendar link and no Klangagenda account required

    • including full recurrence support (daily/weekly/monthly/yearly, interval,
      weekday selection, end date or occurrence count) and an optional image and
      ticket/info link per event. These events are automatically merged with any
      synced calendar events on the frontend.
  • New “Klangagenda Hub” tab: connect the plugin to your own Klangagenda
    account. If your account manages a venue there, the same venue settings and
    usage statistics become available here. If you connect without managing a
    venue, either your calendar link (if configured) or your own events (if not)
    are automatically transmitted to Klangagenda and shown there.

2.5.1

  • Fix: increased spacing below the month heading (introduced in 2.5.0) so it
    no longer sits too close to the following event.

2.5.0

  • The corner radius of the “Tickets kaufen” and “Mehr Termine” buttons is now
    configurable.
  • Font size and color for the event title, date, location and description
    are now individually configurable in the backend.
  • Optional month headings (e.g. “Oktober 2026”) can now be shown between
    events whenever the month changes.

2.4.0

  • The per-event description can now be shown or hidden, and its text color
    is configurable in the backend.
  • When the description is hidden, each event becomes clickable and opens a
    popup with the full event details (title, date, location, description)
    instead – text selection/copying on the rest of the list is unaffected.
  • The “Kalenderansicht” preview cards now also show the description color
    and the popup behavior live.

2.3.2

  • Fix: after automatically (re-)creating the events table (see 2.3.1), the
    calendar is now also synchronized immediately, instead of waiting for the
    next scheduled sync (up to 30 minutes) or a manual click on “Jetzt
    synchronisieren”.

2.3.1

  • Fix: the events database table is now also created/repaired on every
    page load if missing, not only on plugin activation. This prevents
    “table doesn’t exist” errors when the plugin is updated by overwriting
    its files (e.g. via FTP or a hosting file manager) instead of being
    deactivated/reactivated through the WordPress admin.

2.3.0

  • Added three additional card-style calendar views (date on the right with
    an accent-colored left border, date on the left, and a full-height
    accent-colored date block) as alternatives to the standard date badge.
  • New backend section “Kalenderansicht” under Settings to preview all
    available views live (using the currently configured colors, even before
    saving) and select the active one.
  • New configurable card background color for the card-style views.

2.2.0

  • Removed the legacy [google_agenda] / [google_agenda_no_recurring]
    / [google_agenda_konzerte] shortcode aliases introduced in 2.0.0;
    please switch any existing pages to [klangagenda] /
    [klangagenda_no_recurring] / [klangagenda_konzerte].

2.1.0

  • Prepared for release in the WordPress plugin directory (full plugin
    header, GPLv2 license, readme.txt in WordPress.org format, English
    readme, dropped “Plugin” from the plugin name).
  • All internal identifiers (classes, functions, options, database
    table, asset handles, hooks) renamed to a distinctive klanca_ /
    KLANCA_ prefix; settings from the predecessor plugin are migrated
    automatically on activation.
  • webcal:// links are stored/displayed unchanged and automatically
    switched to https:// internally when fetched.
  • Sync interval changed to 30 minutes (custom WP-Cron interval).
  • Frontend hint renamed to “orchestriert von klangagenda.de” and now
    hidden by default; site administrators must actively opt in via a
    checkbox in the settings before it is shown.
  • All CSS and JavaScript are now loaded via wp_enqueue_style() /
    wp_enqueue_script() instead of inline <style>/<script> tags.
  • Hardened output escaping and database queries per WordPress coding
    standards.

2.0.0

  • Renamed to “Klangagenda Calendar Plugin” with its own top-level menu
    item in the WordPress backend.
  • Shortcodes renamed to [klangagenda], [klangagenda_no_recurring],
    [klangagenda_konzerte] (previous [google_agenda] shortcodes remain
    functional for backward compatibility).
  • New “Anleitung” tab with step-by-step instructions per calendar
    provider.
  • Optional “powered by” hint on the frontend, toggleable in the
    backend.

1.3.1

  • Fix: moved asset registration from plugins_loaded to
    wp_enqueue_scripts to avoid a WordPress notice (“headers already
    sent”) when saving other forms.

1.3.0

  • Konzerte shortcode: toggles for ticket button, description, and date
    badge; automatic removal of “(+)”/”(-)” markers from event titles.

1.2.0

  • “Load more” button with AJAX loading and loading animation.
  • Configurable accent/hover colors.

1.1.0

  • Separate concerts shortcode with automatic “buy tickets” button.
  • Fixed date windows (ab/bis) per post.

1.0.0

  • Initial release: Google Calendar agenda view with RRULE support.

short_description: Calendar plugin for embedding a Google, Apple/iCloud, Microsoft 365/Outlook or Konzertmeister calendar as an agenda list. Free from KlangAgenda.de.
description:
Displays a calendar (Google Calendar, Apple Calendar/iCloud, Microsoft 365 /
Outlook Calendar, or Konzertmeister – via iCal/ICS link) as an agenda list,
in the style of “date box on the left, title/date/time/location/description
on the right”. No click behavior (no modal, no redirect) – text remains
normally selectable/copyable.

Provided free of charge by KlangAgenda.de – on
Klangagenda.de you can promote your concerts free of charge across your
region, book rehearsal and concert venues, and offer your own space to
others to make better use of it.

All settings (including a detailed step-by-step guide for each calendar
provider) are available in the WordPress backend under the dedicated
top-level menu “Klangagenda Kalender” (with its own calendar icon).

Shortcodes

[klangagenda]
Shows all upcoming events (including recurring ones, e.g. weekly
rehearsals).

[klangagenda_no_recurring]
Shows upcoming events WITHOUT recurring events (e.g. only
concerts/special events, no weekly rehearsals).

[klangagenda_konzerte]
Shows only events whose title contains the word “Konzert” (German for
“concert”, case-insensitive), e.g. “Winterkonzert”, “Sommerkonzert”,
“Adventskonzert”. By default shows neither a date badge nor a
description per event – instead, the description of the first (next)
event is shown once at the top of the whole list.

By default, this shortcode shows no “Buy tickets” button per event.
The attribute ticket_button="ja" turns this on. beschreibung="nein"
hides the intro description at the top, and badge="ja" shows the date
badge per event:

[klangagenda_konzerte ticket_button="ja" badge="ja" beschreibung="nein"]

“(+)”/”(-)” markers (e.g. from Konzertmeister sync) are automatically
stripped from event titles in all shortcodes.

All shortcodes accept an optional count attribute, e.g.
[klangagenda count=”5″]. If omitted, the default count from the
plugin settings is used.

Fixed date window per post (ab / bis)

Normally the shortcodes automatically show the next upcoming events
from now on. For the typical workflow (one post per concert
tour/period; once it’s over the post moves into the archive and a new
post with the next dates is created), there are optional attributes
ab (from) and bis (until) (format YYYY-MM-DD):

[klangagenda_konzerte ab="2026-09-01" bis="2026-09-14"]

This makes this specific post permanently show exactly the events in
this time window – even once they’re in the past. ab and bis can
also be used individually.

“Load more” button

[klangagenda] and [klangagenda_no_recurring] automatically show a
“Mehr Termine” (load more) button below the list whenever more events
are available beyond the currently shown count. Clicking it loads more
events via AJAX (no page reload). The button does not appear on the
[klangagenda_konzerte] shortcode and can additionally be hidden
explicitly via [klangagenda button="nein"].

“orchestriert von klangagenda.de”

Below each event list (or below the “load more” button, if present),
a subtle, light-gray, centered note “orchestriert von klangagenda.de”
appears by default, linking to https://klangagenda.de. This note can
be fully switched on or off in the backend under “Klangagenda
Kalender”.

Recurring events (RRULE)

RRULE processing covers the common patterns (daily/weekly/monthly/
yearly, interval, count, end date, weekdays). Recurring events without
an end date are pre-calculated up to the configured time horizon
(default 12 months), and continued automatically on the next sync.

Ticket button

The button appears when the title contains “konzert” and the
description contains an http(s) link. Only the first link found is
used.

upgrade_notice.2.9.0: New expandable "Detailansicht" calendar view design, with optional subtitle/ensemble fields and rich-text descriptions for own events, plus a real .ics download button.
upgrade_notice.2.8.0: Konzertmeister category labels ("Auftritt -", "Probe -", etc.) are now hidden from the description text. "Probenanfrage"/"Auftrittsanfrage"/ "Information" events are now hidden by default (new setting to show them).
upgrade_notice.2.7.2: Fixes a bug where a single moved/edited occurrence of a recurring event could appear twice in the list.
upgrade_notice.2.7.1: Klangagenda Hub connection now also pulls back events created directly on Klangagenda.de, with duplicate protection. Requires Kalender-Hub 8.38.0+.
upgrade_notice.2.7.0: Button texts for "Tickets kaufen" and "Mehr Termine" are now configurable in settings. No action needed - existing text stays the same until changed.
upgrade_notice.2.6.4: Fixes all-day events in the [klangagenda_konzerte] shortcode showing their description detached above the list instead of in their own event card.
upgrade_notice.2.6.3: Fixes duplicate events that could appear when both a calendar link and the Klangagenda Hub venue-events display were active.
upgrade_notice.2.6.2: Adds an optional toggle (off by default) to also show other organizations' events at your Hub-managed venue. Existing settings are preserved.
upgrade_notice.2.6.1: Aligns the Klangagenda Hub connection with the actual, already-built Hub API and improves the display of venue settings/statistics. Recommended if you use or plan to use the Hub connection.
upgrade_notice.2.6.0: Adds a backend tab to create your own events (with recurrence and images, no external calendar or Klangagenda account needed) and a tab to connect the plugin to your Klangagenda account. Existing settings and events are preserved.
upgrade_notice.2.5.0: Adds settings for button corner radius, individual font size/color for title, date, location and description, and optional month headings. Existing settings and appearance are preserved.
upgrade_notice.2.4.0: Adds an on/off switch and color setting for the per-event description, plus a click-to-open popup for events when it's hidden. Existing settings (description shown, previous color) are preserved.
upgrade_notice.2.3.2: Events now appear immediately after the automatic table repair from 2.3.1, without waiting for the next scheduled sync.
upgrade_notice.2.3.1: Fixes a "table doesn't exist" database error that could occur after updating the plugin by overwriting its files instead of deactivating/ reactivating it in WordPress.
upgrade_notice.2.3.0: Adds three new selectable card-style calendar views plus a live preview/ selection UI in the backend. Existing settings and the current view (standard) are preserved.
upgrade_notice.2.2.0: Legacy [google_agenda] shortcodes are removed – update any pages still using them to [klangagenda] / [klangagenda_no_recurring] / [klangagenda_konzerte] before updating.
upgrade_notice.2.1.0: Sync interval changes from hourly to every 30 minutes; the frontend hint now reads "orchestriert von klangagenda.de" instead of "powered by klangagenda.de" and is off by default until actively enabled. Existing settings are preserved.
